name: Clement Attlee
role: British Prime Minister (1945–1951) and Labour Party leader (1935–1955)
summary: Attlee was a democratic socialist who sought a classless co-operative commonwealth through public ownership, planning and the welfare state, achieved by constitutional means and without dictatorship of Left or Right. As prime minister he led the nationalisations, the NHS, Indian independence and British entry into NATO, and he backed an independent British atomic bomb. In later life he opposed joining the Common Market, favoured a world rule of law and supported decriminalising homosexuality.

universal-healthcare.rationale: As Prime Minister he told Bevan to prepare a National Health Service scheme as part of the government's programme and led the government that created it in 1948.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Wrote that capitalism is chaos and waste, that Socialists cannot make it work, and in 1954 that his policy was 'not a reformed capitalism but progress towards a democratic socialism'.

public-ownership.rationale: Programme in his book called for taking over the Bank of England, coal, gas, electricity, transport and armaments; as PM he ordered nationalisation of fuel, power, transport, steel and the Bank.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Wrote that inequalities of wealth must be redressed through taxation and that raising income tax with pensions is a move towards equalisation; his government taxed heavily.

unions-good.rationale: Called the Trade Unions the backbone of the Labour movement and was himself a union member; wrote that they win security and status for members.

property-fundamental.rationale: Proposed community ownership of land and major industries, but insisted on compensation and respect for reasonable expectations, so private property was to be overridden by law, not by confiscation.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Argued for planning and control of industry, finance and fuel in the public interest, going well beyond tighter regulation to ownership.

cut-welfare.rationale: Promised to abolish the means test, give pensions and maintenance for the unemployed, and led a government that expanded National Insurance and assistance.

worker-ownership.rationale: Wanted workers to be 'citizens in industry' with a say through their unions, but placed ownership in the community and said the community's interest must come before any sectional group's.

strong-leader.rationale: Condemned the herd mind that seeks an old bull to follow and dictatorship generally.

state-harmful.rationale: Argued the state is needed to prevent oppression and promoted its use for social ends.

decide-locally.rationale: Warned of over-centralisation and called for wide regional decentralisation, including Scotland and Wales, within a national plan.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Said separate nationalities should preserve their culture and that socialism does not ignore peoples' diversities.

gradual-change.rationale: Preferred constitutional change that retains the essential fabric of British government and empirical partial solutions.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Wrote of subordinating national sovereignty to world loyalty and in 1959 urged a rule of law with ceded sovereignty through the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Criticised the Manchester-school ideal of free trade as basis for peace and wanted planned import boards, though welcomed an open door in colonies.

nation-first.rationale: Wrote that nationalism is egotism writ large and that a socialist government cannot pursue policy at others' expense.

revolution-justified.rationale: Rejected violent revolution but allowed that a tyrannical government may justify extra-constitutional resistance.

experts-over-public.rationale: Wrote that a government should not need experts to tell it policy, only to carry out its decisions.

central-planning.rationale: Argued for a national plan covering what is produced, where, and capital direction, while allowing managerial freedom, regional variety and some small private enterprise; in 1961 praised the planning his government did.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Proposed a National Investment Board to direct capital into housing, electrification, transport and new industries and to locate industry in distressed areas.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: His picture of a socialist Britain has workers earning money and 'sufficient money to keep himself and his family', with only approximate, not literal, equality of purchasing power.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Called for converting the Bank of England into a state institution controlling credit, and ordered it nationalised in 1945.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Denounced the Corporate State and any scheme putting society into state-directed bodies; wrote that Labour wants a wide gulf between capitalist democracy and the Corporate State.

one-party-rule.rationale: Rejected dictatorship of either Left or Right and insisted on an Opposition.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: In 1936 praised constitutional kingship as a democratic rallying point of stability; never proposed abolition.

democracy-best.rationale: Argued democracy is better than dictatorship even though it means liberty to make mistakes.

direct-votes.rationale: Refused in 1945 to introduce the referendum, saying it was alien to British tradition and an instrument of Nazism and Fascism.

workers-councils.rationale: Wanted to preserve the British parliamentary machinery and rejected Soviet-style methods.

right-to-secede.rationale: Accepted partition of India by local vote but later said India should have stayed united.

natural-rulers.rationale: Wrote that no human beings are fit to hold absolute power and that Socialism seeks to abolish classes.

political-violence-never.rationale: Rejected violence as a means of change in Britain but accepted force against aggression and coups.

war-builds-character.rationale: Regarded war as an evil and its use only to avoid a greater evil; saw the H-bomb as threatening civilisation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Said society has been careful to separate the ecclesiastical idea of sin from crime.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Praised Britain as three races combined in a larger unity and defended equal partnership regardless of colour.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Wrote that British Socialists do not adopt class war as a theory of society and rejected cast-iron theories of historical necessity.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Wrote that the aim of the Socialist State must be equality and ultimately substantial economic equality.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Wrote that land in the colonies should be held in trust for the natives and every native family assured of land.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Wrote of replacing the motive of competition with that of service.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Said Labour must work empirically but also held that socialism is a faith and principle, not just machinery.

direct-action.rationale: Wrote that as long as the ballot box is available workers have no right to seek ends by other means.

means-match-ends.rationale: Argued violent revolution implies the totalitarian state and that democratic ends need democratic methods.

production-for-use.rationale: Described the essential change under socialism as a change of motive from profit to service and wrote of production to meet needs.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Spoke of the exploitation of workers by capitalists and of wage slavery, though he rejected a simple two-class theory and said many capitalists perform useful service.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rejected class dictatorship and terrorism and said the Labour Party is democratic.

collective-farming.rationale: Planned both groups of smallholders and large public farming corporations, so neither wholly collective nor wholly individual farming.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Wrote that imperialism is the form capitalism takes towards other nations and that economic causes of war must be removed, but did not hold a world war between systems inevitable.

harm-principle.rationale: Said the law should not treat as crime what is a matter of sin, in supporting homosexual law reform.

conscription.rationale: Led the government that introduced peacetime national service and called his 1939 opposition to conscription a mistake.

positive-liberty.rationale: Argued liberty is denied by poverty and lack of time and money, so socialism gives freedom.

total-state.rationale: Wrote that British Socialists never made an idol of the State and reject the beehive or ants' nest.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Condemned imperialism and the idea that nations should expand, calling for a world commonwealth.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Wrote of introducing democracy into industry, with workers and consumers taking part in management of socialised industries.

national-self-determination.rationale: Wrote that each nation may regulate its own affairs and as PM ended British rule in India, Burma and Ceylon.

force-without-un.rationale: Argued in 1956 that Britain was not entitled to use force outside the United Nations and criticised the Suez operation.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rejected partnership with employers (the Mond-Turner talks) and said society involves class struggle, while denying that violent class war is needed.

workers-nation.rationale: Said the Labour Party must act nationally and rejected the idea that class interests deny national action.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Said in 1961 that apartheid denies the fundamental principles of the Commonwealth.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Said finance and the Lords serve the capitalist order, yet that the machinery of government has passed between classes and can be used for socialism.

proportional-representation.rationale: In 1958 asked a Lords questioner whether he had noticed across the Channel the disadvantages of many small parties with no principles.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Inferred: his statements on equal brotherhood and rejection of race superiority are incompatible with discouraging mixed marriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Wrote that Labour applies the brotherhood of man and does not admit that the white race has a right of primogeniture.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Held that democracy means the right to change policy and personnel of government, otherwise no true freedom.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Aimed at the substitution of the motive of service for that of competition.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Described wage workers as under orders and wage slaves, and freedom as limited by power over them.

vanguard-party.rationale: Wrote that the Communist Party believes in rule by an active minority, an ideological aristocracy, which is undemocratic.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Programme put the unemployed, low-paid, ill-housed and old first and aimed to level up the lowest standards of life.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Wrote that low standards of life are not caused by inability of the community to produce but by failure to use available resources under capitalism.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Defended wartime and postwar controls and rationing as necessary against profiteering and said it was hard to argue they should lapse in peace.

party-controls-media.rationale: Said no forcible suppression of opinion and criticised Nazi universities as parrot cages.

party-commands-army.rationale: Wrote that armed forces should not be politicised and remain loyal to whatever government is in power.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Defended the party pledge and the duty of members to carry out majority decisions, subject to conscience abstention.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Backed ceding sovereignty for world peace but opposed entry into the Common Market in 1961-62, objecting to losing control of planning and to the Treaty of Rome.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred: his writing puts defence under civilian Ministers responsible to Parliament, not a head of state choosing ministers.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Rejected the class-war view that workers should obstruct their own government in war.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: As PM he supported the Marshall Plan and promoted NATO and kept British forces abroad.

people-in-arms.rationale: Wanted a democratised professional force with officers drawn from the ranks, not a citizen militia.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Described with approval the UN effort to unify Korea and the aim of Korean unity.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Wrote that the wealth of society is variety not uniformity and warned of the reformer's tyranny.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: On India wrote that nationalism is not enough and handing peasants to their own capitalists is no gain, so economic power must also be shifted.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Wrote that the standard of life of Asia and Africa must be raised and world resources developed for all peoples.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Was prime mover in the 1947 decision to build a British bomb and refused full dependence on the US, but in 1963 doubted Polaris.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Wanted the Bank of England brought under ministerial control so credit policy follows government policy.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Said land and major industries should be owned for the community and that the community's interest must come before any sectional group's.

collective-defense.rationale: Wrote that an attack on any member must be treated as an attack on all, and promoted NATO as PM.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: His tribute to George V praised a sovereign who gave society a rallying point of stability above party.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred: his insistence on democracy and rule of law implies no ruler is above the law.

leader-cult.rationale: Did not want a party where obedience to a leader stifles free thought and condemned the herd and old bull.

land-redistribution.rationale: Wanted land owned by the community, not given to farmers, but also planned smallholdings and settlement.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Wrote that Britain's nationalities should be given weight to preserve their own culture and develop their national life.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Wrote that the Communist tendency to reduce all history to an economic formula has always been rejected.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Rejected the Ottawa agreements and any attempt to make the Empire an exclusive economic unit.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Described the Labour programme of world control of hours and conditions of labour and common standards through the League.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Rejected terrorism and minority seizure of power.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Opposed the powers of the hereditary Lords and wanted class distinctions abolished, but accepted an earldom in 1955.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Held that where peoples were not ready for self-government Britain should act as trustee under League supervision, while aiming at self-government as soon as possible.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred: his view that the elected Commons' will must prevail over Lords implies no entrenched limits on it.

minority-veto.rationale: Rejected the view that a dissenting minority can block the majority and said the movement must accept majority rule.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Wrote that if a government defies its pledges and persecutes, resistance outside constitutional action may be justified.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Wanted the elected Commons' will to prevail over the Lords and the Crown's role limited to constitutional kingship.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Said colonies had been exploited for imperial profit and that exploitation of one territory by another must end.

party-own-road.rationale: Said the Labour and Socialist International cannot give orders to national parties and criticised Communists for obeying the Comintern.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Condemned dictatorship of the Left or Right equally, naming both Berlin and Moscow models and terror under Communist Russia as well as Fascism.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Wrote there is objection to transplanting British institutions into soil where they cannot flourish, but insisted on widest franchise.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Wrote that supreme authority for defence must be civilian and that nothing is worse than the political general.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Wrote that the party pledge does not turn a representative into a mere delegate, though party members take part in decisions that bind them.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Argued the nation should provide adequate pensions to those who have worked, rather than leave them dependent on their own savings.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Wrote that land will be owned by the community, with citizens having reasonable security of tenure, not exactly the 'only while used' condition.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Said life is more than material success and that capitalism makes people content with narrow standards.

corporate-influence.rationale: Wrote that financial interests assert themselves against the government and tariffs reflect private interests' pressure.

job-guarantee.rationale: Wrote that under Socialism anyone capable of working is certain of a job and that when demand for his labour ends he is given other work; also proposed public works for the unemployed.

non-intervention.rationale: Wrote that interference in another country's internal affairs, as in Spain, is a new form of aggression and that states should abstain from interfering.

informal-organisation.rationale: Stressed disciplined party organisation and union structure rather than small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Argued for compulsory arbitration, an international court and surrender of absolute sovereignty to a world authority.

defeat-communism.rationale: In 1954 and 1959 urged coexistence-minded talks with the USSR, while resisting Communist aggression through NATO and in Korea.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Rejected both Fascism and Communism as the only choices and presented democratic socialism as another course, while opposing capitalism too.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Supported the Sexual Offences Bill in 1965, said the Labouchere law should go, that homosexuality is not cured by crime law and that blackmail is the greater evil; helped found the Homosexual Law Reform Society.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Said there will be no forcible suppression of adverse opinion under Socialism and that dictatorship is police-ridden.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Wrote that Labour rejects the colonial empire as an exclusive field of exploitation by British capital.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Wrote that citizens must actively participate through voluntary societies, democratic industry and control of immediate activities.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Rejected a popular front and said the issue is Socialism versus Capitalism, not a combination of best ideas.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred: grounded democratic authority in popular consent and was agnostic.

social-market-economy.rationale: Rejected a reformed capitalism with social protection as his aim, wanting socialism, though his government kept a mixed economy in practice.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Called complete abolition of armed forces an ideal for some day but rejected disarmament by example.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Committed Britain to NATO and the Atlantic alliance against the Soviet bloc.

property-franchise.rationale: Praised the move to a franchise based on citizenship and not property ownership.

racial-franchise.rationale: Wrote that Labour will insist on the widest franchise in the colonies and condemned minority white rule.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Argued the power of wealth, including the City of London, can override the elected government and that liberty is restricted by poverty and property power.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: His East End social work led him to conclude that the causes of poverty required Socialism and state action, not charity.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Wrote that socialists never wanted men and women drilled and regimented.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Endorsed the Party objective of securing the full fruits of industry for those working by hand or brain and distinguished earned from unearned income in taxation.

independent-unions.rationale: Said the Party is the partner, not the servant, of the TUC and criticised Communist-run industrial tactics, while the unions keep freedom in their own sphere.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Wanted transport and fuel public and praised municipal and state services; hospitals and local services were to be built and run publicly.

second-chamber.rationale: In 1957 said he now believed in a revising second chamber, though one that must not thwart the elected Commons.

person-over-state.rationale: Wrote that Socialism aims to give greater freedom to the individual and individuals should not be sacrificed to the State.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Wrote that economic activity is only the foundation for a full life of the spirit.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Said armed force is only for resisting aggression and for collective action under the League or UN, yet as PM sent forces to Korea and Malaya.

arms-reduction.rationale: Called for reducing armaments to the lowest level by international agreement and in 1954 moved for a summit to control armaments.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Served in the army and wrote that war resistance applies only to a government that is an aggressor; supported the war effort in 1914 and 1939.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Described unions as concerned with wages, hours and conditions through agreements and said unions would help set conditions in socialised industry.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Wrote that with the existing machinery of government the fundamental changes can be made.

sacred-nation.rationale: Called nationalism egotism writ large and 'National Socialism' a contradiction.

farm-price-support.rationale: Said his government acted to sustain British agriculture, and his book proposed marketing boards and land drainage for farmers.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Government built British atomic bomb and in 1955 said 'there is no defence' so we rely on deterrents; later doubted the need.

workers-own-party.rationale: Wrote that the Labour Party rests on independent working-class representation.

women-suffrage.rationale: In his tribute to George V praised giving the vote to practically every man and woman.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Said decentralisation was needed for Scotland and Wales and that nationalities should preserve their culture.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: His India plan let provincial legislators and local referenda in Sylhet and the NWFP decide partition and allegiance.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Promised to abolish the means test and favoured universal pensions and services rather than aid limited to the poorest.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Defended party discipline and parliament and opposed rule by leaders over parties.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Argued workers value their British liberties and that it is false to say it does not matter whether they are ruled by British or foreign capitalists.

notes: Positions on India, empire, nuclear weapons and European integration changed over time: in 1937 he called for trusteeship and League supervision of colonies, in 1947 he ended British rule in India; he built the British bomb in 1947 but doubted Polaris in 1963; he urged collective security in the 1930s and promoted NATO after 1949. Immigration, capital punishment and abortion are left null because no personal statement was found. The 1945 manifesto was used only where he personally championed a policy.
